settings.heading: The Letter Tray
settings.intro: No wheel, no whistles. Three envelopes on the hall tray, each sealed with wax, each with something small inside. Choose one and the house will tell you afterwards what the others held.
settings.hint: Choose an envelope. The house does not shuffle twice.
settings.repeat_text: This is the envelope you opened. The house keeps a record.
settings.terms: One favour to a household, and one only — the house would notice. Codes last until the last post for Christmas and do not stack.

settings.heading: The Christmas Edition
settings.intro: Not a gift guide — a short list. Each piece is made to order and numbered to its edition, so the one you send is the one we cut for you.

settings.note: Further afield, and the longer way round.
Yours is cut after you ask for it. The clock starts then.
The Chaperone ships when the edition opens, not before.

settings.heading: The last post
settings.intro: Nothing here sits in a warehouse waiting to be wanted, so the house posts these dates rather than hurrying you. Order by them and it arrives before the morning.
settings.closing: After the last post the house still sends — just not in time. We will write and tell you so before you spend a cent.

settings.body:
December is the month people stop using the good things in case they are needed for something better. The good glass stays in the cabinet. The nice paper is saved. The bath oil waits for an occasion that never quite declares itself.

This house takes the opposite view, and always has. Nothing here is being kept for later — not the suede, not the linen, not the ribbon. Count the days if you like. We will be using ours.

settings.heading: The Christmas list
settings.text: One letter a week through December: what has been cut, what is nearly gone, and when the last post falls. No countdown timers in your inbox — we save the clock for the page.
settings.note: We write rarely and beautifully. Unsubscribe whenever, no hard feelings.
